--- title: Methodology bread-crumbs: false --- Raw pageviews have two problems: Wikipedia wide traffic has drifted since 2015, and topics live on different scales. The index normalizes twice. ``` views_per_million = article_views / total_project_views x 1e6 smoothed = rolling 28 day median nostalgia_index = smoothed / baseline_median x 100 ``` The baseline is the first 12 months of each series. A revival event is a day where the unsmoothed index exceeds 3x the trailing 90 day median. Caveats: data starts 2015-07-01; only `agent=user` traffic is used (spiders excluded); redirects are resolved through the MediaWiki API; topics without an article in 2015 have no true baseline, so their index is relative to their first year. ## Worked example ::: {#55a37870 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd from nostalgia_index import NostalgiaIndex views = pd.read_csv("fixtures/views.csv", parse_dates=["date"]) totals = pd.read_csv("fixtures/totals.csv", parse_dates=["date"]) ni = NostalgiaIndex() idx = ni.compute(views, totals) ni.summary(idx).round(1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` /tmp/ipykernel_16195/1864511853.py:8: UserWarning: obj.round has no effect with datetime, timedelta, or period dtypes.
